summary: Relief bounce that ran out of gas. A strong October jobs report, 165,000 added with unemployment back to 4.1 percent, snapped the washout and the Nasdaq rallied to reclaim its trailing stop, closing up 1.24 percent at 27,075. But the bounce lost steam: MNQ faded off a 27,425 early high all the way back inside the opening range and closed below its session VWAP. The S&P tagged along for only plus 0.25 percent and never reclaimed its own stop, so the broad market has not confirmed the turn. The strong number pulled the safe-haven trade out of gold, down 0.83 percent to 4,075, and crude gave back an overnight pop to finish roughly flat. Fear eased but did not leave: VIX slid about 8 percent to 25.6, still well above its pre-washout teens.

setups.name: AVWAP Back Into Range (BIR)
setups.entry: Fade the failed opening-range break on the full-body close back inside the range.
setups.stop: Beyond the break extreme (the 27,425 spike high today).
setups.t1: The opposite side of the opening range, then NYVWAP.
setups.bias: The day's cleanest structure. Price broke the OR up at 14:45 UTC, failed, and closed back inside at 14:54, the textbook BIR. No CPI or Monday block Friday, so it was eligible and it fired. Note BIR is blocked next session (Monday).

setups.name: AVWAP Deviation Band
setups.entry: Fade a stretched tag of the plus or minus 2 to 3 sigma band back toward the session VWAP.
setups.bias: A two-sided exhaustion day: price pushed beyond both 3 sigma bands and reverted each time, which is the reversion edge's home. Unlike yesterday's one-way trend where the bands got ridden, today they held. Size for the still-wide ranges.

setups.name: AVWAP Midrange (MID)
setups.entry: Fade rejection wicks at the OR edges back toward the middle, 9:30 to 10:30 ET only.
setups.bias: After the failed breakout, price chopped between the opening range and NYVWAP, the range the MID play works. The early move was a breakout attempt and the window is first-hour only, so it is borderline rather than clean.

setups.name: TSMOM-20
setups.entry: Trend-follow each board on its own ATR stop.
setups.stop: MNQ long above 26,801; MES short below 7,467.
setups.t1: MNQ the 27,481 50-hour line; MES the session low.
setups.bias: The trend signal is split: MNQ reclaimed its stop and flipped long while MES is still below its stop, so there is no agreed one-way trend to follow. A divergence like this is a caution flag for the trend-follower; keep size light until the two boards agree.

event.name: October jobs report (nonfarm payrolls) printed Friday Nov 6, 8:30 AM ET: 165,000 added, unemployment 4.1 percent
event.consensus: Economists looked for a modest gain after recent cooling (consensus around plus 50,000). The print more than doubled expectations.
event.actual: Plus 165,000 nonfarm payrolls for October, unemployment rate 4.1 percent. A clear upside surprise against a low bar.
event.surprise: Positive, risk-on. A strong labor number eased the fear from Thursday's washout and pulled the safe-haven bid out of gold. The reaction was a gap-up and a stop reclaim that then faded.
event.nqReaction: NQ gapped up and reclaimed its 26,801 trailing stop, spiked to 27,425 in the first fifteen minutes, then faded all afternoon back inside the opening range to close 27,075, up 1.24 percent, below NYVWAP 27,184 and the 27,481 50-hour average.
event.crossAsset: MES only plus 0.25 percent at 7,400 and still below its 7,467 stop, the laggard. December gold minus 0.83 percent at 4,075 as the haven bid unwound. December crude minus 0.13 percent at 90.59, giving back an overnight pop to 92.55 and losing its 91.47 stop. VIX about 25.6, down roughly 8 percent.

risk.dailyLossBudget: Treat as guarded on a two-sided relief-bounce tape.

risk.openRisk: The equity trend is split: MNQ flipped long above 26,801 while MES is still below 7,467, so there is no agreed direction. Gold lost the 4,100 round and sits on its 50-hour line; crude lost its stop. The open still moved a wide range fast, so respect gap and slippage risk into next week's CPI.
risk.note: Throttle state REDUCED, eased from DEFENSIVE. Volatility is coming down but is not back to normal: MNQ ATR(14) fell to 213.75 from 262.76 and VIX slid to 25.6 from 27.77, so keep per-trade size trimmed against stops that are still wide. The equity trend is split, MNQ flipped long above its 26,801 stop while MES is still below 7,467, so TSMOM has no agreed direction; trade each board on its own signal and keep size light until they agree. The E3v2 long-only gate stays shut with price below the EMA50. Today's lesson for the budget: the relief-bounce chase is the fastest way to give back yesterday's discipline, so wait for acceptance above the line before adding risk. Week ahead: the October CPI prints Tuesday Nov 10 at 8:30 AM ET (still shutdown-contingent, though Friday's jobs report did print), Veterans Day is Wednesday Nov 11 with the bond market closed and equity futures open, and the next policy event is the December FOMC.

psychology: After a scary day, the bounce is the trap. Yesterday's crash makes a strong jobs number feel like the all-clear, and the urge is to chase the open and get it back fast. Today punished that: price spiked to 27,425 in the first fifteen minutes, then spent the rest of the day fading back into the range. The traders who did well let the move come to their level instead of chasing the gap. When the tape is still two-sided and the S&P has not even reclaimed its stop, treat a bounce as just a bounce until price proves the turn with acceptance above the line. Patience is the edge on a relief day. If you are still shaken from yesterday, smaller size and fewer trades is how you stay in the game.

fullReport.title: NY Opening Range / HTA OPEN (MNQ)
fullReport.html:
Failed up-break, back-into-range day. OR High 27,308, OR Low 27,035.75, Width 272.25 pts.

Anchored at the 14:30 UTC NY cash open (EST, after daylight saving ended Nov 1). The first 15 minutes set a 272 point range off a 27,168.25 open. Price broke the range to the upside at 14:45 UTC with a 27,344.75 close, spiked to a 27,425 high (the prior-day stop), then rolled over and printed a full-body close back inside the range at 14:54, a textbook Back-In-Range (BIR) setup. There was no down-break. The 20:00 UTC cash-close bar finished 27,075.25, back inside the opening range and below NYVWAP 27,183.53. Friday blocks nothing, so BIR, HOF, MID and BNC were all eligible; the structure was the failed-breakout BIR, not the short-side hand-off. Volume is disclaimed on the continuous contract, so VWAP uses a typical-price mean.

fullReport.title: Momentum Breakout (Regime Filter)
fullReport.html:
Gate RED, long-only edge blocked. Price closed 27,075, still below EMA(50) at 27,481, with ROC(12) back to plus 0.14 percent.

RVOL is not available (volume disclaimed on the continuous contract). Momentum ticked from deeply negative back toward flat on the bounce, but the regime gate needs price to accept above the 50-hour line before the E3v2 long-only breakout can fire. With price under the EMA50, the long gate stays shut, which is the filter doing its job: it will not chase a relief bounce that has not yet proven itself.

The close 27,075.25 sits just under the minus 2 sigma band, stretched to the downside into the bell. Unlike yesterday's one-way trend where the bands got ridden, today the bands held, so fades of a stretched touch back toward the 27,174 mean were in habitat. Size for the still-wide ranges.

The strong jobs number pulled the safe-haven bid; gold lost the 4,100 round and the 4,075 average, cooled to the 4,050 zone exactly as the row warned (overnight 4,032, RTH low 4,052.5), and closed 4,075 on the line.

But it gave the move back into the cash close, finished 90.59 and lost its risen 91.47 trailing stop, so the named levels held while the trend flipped short by the bell.

yesterdaysMapScore.note: Published Nov 5 for the Friday Nov 6 session. The map hedged the washout continuing against a reclaim. Friday delivered a strong jobs report and a relief bounce that faded: MNQ reclaimed its stop but gave the move back inside the range (mixed), MES stayed the laggard below its stop (mixed), gold's losing-4,075 branch played out as the haven bid came off, and crude held its levels but gave the pop back and lost its stop (mixed).
